messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 2173456789 - GPU pool 'spot-usw2' reporting capacity_exhaustion. queue length > 1200, errors > 5% for last 3m. auto-escalate: oncall-ml@jess, oncall-infra@alex. runbook: /runbooks/gpu-capacity-fallback

pagerduty: PAGER: paging jess (oncall-ml) - high severity incident (gpu-capacity).

jess (oncall-ml): ack. I'm pulling queue metrics and autoscaler logs now. tagging chris for visibility.

alex (oncall-infra): joining. seeing large number of spot node preemptions over the last 7m: ~45% of spot-usw2 nodes marked terminated. autoscaler desired=12, current=8, max=8 -> hpa at cap. suspect quota/limit preventing scale up.

kevin (sre): can you paste the HPA/cluster-autoscaler events? I want to confirm if CA is throttled or hitting provider limits.

alex (oncall-infra): pasted logs:
```
$ kubectl describe hpa gpu-pool-spot -n inference
Name: gpu-pool-spot
Min replicas: 2
Max replicas: 8
Replicas: 8 current / 8 desired
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From                         Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----                         -------
  Warning  FailedRescale      5m    cluster-autoscaler          Failed to scale up: quotaExceeded error: You have reached your GPU quota in region us-west-2
```

jess (oncall-ml): that matches queue growth. Requests are piling up into the generation queue. Latency for in-flight requests jumped 3x, some timeouts returning 503. Support dashboard shows ~72 customers impacted (mostly mid-tier).

support-bot: 72 conversations flagged as degraded by support rules. see https://redwood/support/alerts/2173456789

chris (eng-lead): summary: autoscaler max set too low for this pattern + quota prevented further scale. fallback path should route to dedicated-gpu-1 (on-demand) but I see no fallbacks in effect. Is routing policy broken?

alex (oncall-infra): investigating router logs. quick check:
```
$ curl -s https://router.internal/policy/spot-usw2 | jq .fallback
{ "enabled": false, "target": "dedicated-gpu-1", "matcher": "tag:spot-convert==true" }
```
Fallback disabled due to an earlier experiment flag flip. that explains no automatic failover.

jess (oncall-ml): ok immediate mitigations: (1) manually lift HPA max to 20 if quota allows, (2) if quota blocks, manually trigger on-demand fallback by flipping router fallback to enabled, (3) start draining long-running jobs to low-priority pool. I'll attempt #1 now.

alex (oncall-infra): trying to bump HPA max -> CLI shows cloud provider GPU quota = 12 (hard). bump rejected.

kevin (sre): quota is org-level. we can request increase but that is slow. proceed with routing fallback manual enable. alex, can you toggle the routing flag?

alex (oncall-infra): toggling fallback flag now.
```
$ curl -X POST -d '{"enabled":true}' https://router.internal/policy/spot-usw2/fallback -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***'
{"status":"ok","applied_by":"alex","applied_at":"2026-03-15T14:08:12Z"}
```

incident-bot: action recorded: routing.fallback.enabled by alex at 2026-03-15T14:08:12Z.

jess (oncall-ml): good. initiating manual route shift to dedicated-gpu-1 for new requests. old queue items still bound to spot-usw2 processes. I'll start issuing a controlled reroute: set router weight dedicated=0.6, spot=0.4.

alex (oncall-infra): applied weights. monitoring traffic.

support-bot: customer-impact update: 72 affected -> new customers showing recovery signals. alerting customer success for accounts with SLAs.

kevin (sre): still seeing queue drains slow. some jobs can't migrate due to pinned model shards on spot nodes. we should trigger a temporary scale-up of the dedicated pool (launch new on-demand instances). starting instance boot.

alex (oncall-infra): launching +4 on-demand instances via infra console. ETA ~4m.

jess (oncall-ml): added a hot-cache prewarm job to copy model shards to new nodes to avoid cold-start penalties.

(4m pass)

alex (oncall-infra): on-demand instances came up. routing weights steady. queue length decreasing from 1200 -> 260 over 9m. 503 rate down to 0.8%.

chris (eng-lead): great. what's root cause next? two components: (A) unusually high spot preemptions reduced available capacity, (B) fallback had been disabled by experiment flag and autoscaler max was set low relative to potential peak.

jess (oncall-ml): agree. immediate followups: - revert experiment change gating fallback (we enabled it manually) - raise HPA max from 8 to 20 after quota increase requested - add guardrail: if nodes preempted > 30% in 5m, auto-enable fallback (fail-open)

kevin (sre): I'll open a Jira: INFRA-4421 "runbook: ensure fallback can never be disabled in prod by experiment flag" and assign to alex.

alex (oncall-infra): assigned. also filing quota request with cloud provider (CR-2026-03-15).

support-bot: post-incident customer impact summary drafted: 72 impacted accounts, peak 503s at 6.2%, median latency increase 3x for 8 minutes. will share to CS and APAC teams.

jess (oncall-ml): rolling off oncall in 10m, handing to kevin for post-incident followups. kevin, you got it?

kevin (sre): I got it. compiling timeline and assigning owners. will coordinate postmortem.

chris (eng-lead): thanks everyone. action items: (1) alex: enforce fallback flag removal from experiment and add monitoring (due EOD), (2) kevin: own postmortem and runbook edits (due 72h), (3) jess: verify hot-cache prewarm effectiveness and add to optimize playbook (due 3d).

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2173456789 status -> mitigated. monitored for 30m with stable queue and <1% errors. auto-close scheduled in 24h pending postmortem.

kevin (sre): closing channel for live ops. will reopen if any regression. thanks team. :heart:
